native component FlatString

import String.{maxLeafSize, concatAndBalanceIfNecessary, CatString, spaces}
import Stream.{...}

export FlatString


private language="java"
private package="com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim"

lineSeparator: String = LineSeparator()

private natLineSeparator(): String = builtinPrimitive(
            "com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.lineSeparator")

private LineSeparator(): String =do
    ignore(FlatString); (* This initializes the constructor for FlatString
                   before its type is used (in the next line). *)
    natLineSeparator()
  end

object FlatString extends { String, DelegatedIndexed⟦Char, ZZ32⟧ }
    getter size() : ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen")
    getter asExprString() : String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.asExprString")
    getter asFlatString(): String = self
    getter asString(): String = self
    getter asDebugString(): String = asDebugStringIndented(0)
    getter depth():ZZ32 = 0

    (* With the help of trait DelegatedIndex, this defines our generate method *)
    getter generator() : Generator⟦Char⟧ =
        self.indices.map⟦Char⟧(fn (i:ZZ32):Char ⇒ self.get(i))

    getter isBalanced():Boolean = true
    getter isAlmostBalanced():Boolean = true
    getter isExtremelyUnbalanced():Boolean = false

    balanced():String = self

    opr |self| : ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen")

    uncheckedSubstring(r1: Range⟦ZZ32⟧) : String = do
    (* We could build a subString node here, but not until everything is working,
        because that will introduce
       SubString objects into code that may still expect FlatStrings.
       As written, this method always answers a FlatString.
       In any case, the FlatString object supports substring without copying*)
        assert((r1 ∩ self.bounds).isEmpty, r1.isEmpty,
                    "Empty substring of non-empty string")
        if r1.isEmpty then ""
        else self.javaSubstr(r1.left.get, r1.right.get + 1)    (* Java substr's endIndex is one past the last character *)
        end
    end

    opr =(self, other: FlatString): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Eq")
    opr <(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) < 0
    opr <=(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) ≤ 0
    opr >(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) > 0
    opr >=(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) ≥ 0
    opr CMP(self, other: FlatString): TotalComparison =  self.cmp(other) CMP 0
    opr CMP(self, other:String):TotalComparison = INVERSE (other CMP self)
    opr CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP(self, other:FlatString): TotalComparison =
      self.cicmp(other) CMP 0
    opr CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP(self, other:String): TotalComparison = INVERSE (other CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP self)

    (** get skips bounds checking. **)
    get(i:ZZ32): Char =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.charAt")
    cmp(other:FlatString): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.compareTo")
    cicmp(other:FlatString): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.compareToIgnoreCase")
    javaSubstr(lo:ZZ32,hi:ZZ32): String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaSubstr")
    javaSubstr(lo:ZZ32): String = javaSubstr(lo, self.size)
    javaIndexOf(c:Char): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.indexOf")
    flatConcat(self, b:FlatString):String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeConcatenate")
    flatConcat(self, b:Char):String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Concat")
    javaRegExpMatches(m:FlatString): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaRegExpMatches")
    javaRegExpSplit(m:FlatString, i:ZZ32): String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaRegExpSplit")

    indexOf(c:Char): Maybe⟦ZZ32⟧ = do
        i = javaIndexOf(c)
        if i = -1 then Nothing⟦ZZ32⟧ else Just⟦ZZ32⟧(i) end
      end

    verify():() = do
        assert(self.depth, 0, self)
    end

    asDebugStringIndented(indent: ZZ32): String =
        spaces(indent) || "J" |self| "/" self.depth ":" self

    opr ∈(c:Char, self): Boolean = self.javaIndexOf(c) ≠ -1

    rangeContains(r: Range⟦ZZ32⟧, c: Char):Boolean = self.javaIndexOf(c) ∈ self.bounds[r]

    (** The operator %||% with at least one String argument converts to string and
        concatenates **)
    opr ||(self, b:FlatString): String = do
        if b.isEmpty then self
        elif self.size + b.size > maxLeafSize then
             (* Since both self and b have depth 0, balancing can't be necessary *)
            CatString(self, b)
        else
            flatConcat(self, b)
        end
      end

    opr ||(self, b:String):String = do
        if self.isEmpty then b
        elif b.isEmpty then self
        elif self.size + b.size > maxLeafSize then
            concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, b)
        else
            typecase b.asFlatString of
                f:FlatString ⇒ flatConcat(self, f)
                f:String ⇒ concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, b)
            end
        end
    end

    opr ||(self, b:Char): String =
        if |self| ≥ maxLeafSize then
            concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, b.asString)
        else
            flatConcat(self, b)
        end

    splitWithOffsets():ZeroIndexed⟦(ZZ32, String)⟧ = Nothing⟦(ZZ32, String)⟧
    split():Generator⟦String⟧ = Nothing⟦String⟧

    writeOn(stream: WriteStream): () = stream.write(self)

end FlatString

end

"""mech.py CHUNK_DIR [--final]

The ledger pass's mechanical check of a chunk's new lines, read-only on the tree and the ledger. It reads
the writer's files (rows.rewrite, dups.txt, closes.txt), or with --final the judge's (final.rewrite,
final.dups, final.closes), and the lines the run read (evidence/N.md and the run's rows.tsv files), and
writes mech.md (with --final, mech-final.md) in the chunk's folder. Without --final it also writes
clean.txt, the rewritten lines and the text a duplicate adds, cell by cell, for the cold reader.

For each new line: the template (ledger.py's own lint, as `check --rows`); the lengths; each cited path
and file:line at the base, and whether the cited lines hold the backticked words of the citation's
sentence; each commit hash, resolved and in the base; the reproducer; the row's line now against the line
the run read (the landing's guard); and the tokens of the old line that the new line lacks (paths, rows,
F- and P- entries, backticked names), a list for the checker, not a verdict. For each close: the commit is
in the base, the test is one `ledger.py close` takes, a CONTESTED row names what settled it. For each
duplicate: both rows open, and the kept row's notes and line within their limits with the added text.
Then the chunk applied on copies of the ledger and its history in the chunk's mech-copy/ (apply.py
--keep-going), and `ledger.py check` and `ledger.py check --base BASE` on the copies.
Last line: "MECH: N lines, F failing, every check passes." or "... F failing: ..." with the rows.
"""
import os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys
import common as C

L = C.L
if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    sys.exit(__doc__)
D = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1]).rstrip('/')
FINAL = '--final' in sys.argv
RUN = os.path.dirname(D)
BASE = open(os.path.join(RUN, 'run', 'base.txt')).read().strip()
tree = C.Tree(BASE)
led_base = C.ledger_at(BASE)
led_now = C.ledger_now()
numbers = {r.num for r in led_now.rows}
linter = L.Linter(C.ROOT, numbers)
names = ('final.rewrite', 'final.dups', 'final.closes') if FINAL else ('rows.rewrite', 'dups.txt', 'closes.txt')
read = {}
for x in os.listdir(RUN):
    p = os.path.join(RUN, x, 'rows.tsv')
    if os.path.exists(p):
        for ln in open(p):
            f = ln.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
            if len(f) >= 2 and f[0].isdigit():
                read[int(f[0])] = f[1]


def old_line(n):
    """The line as the run read it: from the evidence file where there is one, else the base's."""
    for x in sorted(os.listdir(RUN)):
        p = os.path.join(RUN, x, 'evidence', '%d.md' % n)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            for ln in open(p, encoding='utf-8'):
                if re.match(r'\| *%d *\|' % n, ln):
                    return ln.rstrip('\n')
    hits = led_base.find(n)
    return hits[0].line if hits else None

### Overloading and the Meet Rule (4)

6. **The Meet Rule's closed-trait case for generic families.** Item 26 gave the Meet Rule a case for two closed traits: declarations over the listed types cover their intersection. The text applies it to declarations with static parameters too; the checker refuses it there. Since batch 8, the functional-method form is accepted and dies at run time (row 566); the function form is still refused.
   - Landed: The text as batch 7b's rung S wrote it; the checker's refusal gated by expected failures; Appendix I names row 546 among the checker's departures.
   - The other way: Scope the text to declarations without static parameters until their coverage is proved; the proof addendum leaves generic families to later work.
   - Its cost: Keeping the text means a checker rung to follow, with the run-time dispatch defect of row 566. Scoping it is a text revision in the S1 form.
   - Home: PLAN, "Climb batch 7b, listed for his review", gather.1; PLAN, "Climb batch 8, listed for his review", Stop met and lifted; PLAN-history, "Climb batch 7b, listed for his review", Stop met and lifted; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/RECORD.md`, rung S; `compile-ladder/rung-overloading-checker/REPORT.md:80` (section 5); row 546 (10-02: 27)
   - Needed by: before microGPT compiles; keeping the text commits a checker rung beside row 566's run-time dispatch defect, which is phase 5's line (PLAN, phase 5).

9. **Exclusion through a bound, and `tint` (row 786).** Do two parameter types exclude each other when the only static arguments at which they could meet are ones a bound rules out? Walk loads `tint[\T extends Red\](x: Box[\T\])` beside `tint[\T extends Blue\](x: Box[\T\])`, reading two type parameters whose bounds exclude as never one type, and the checker refuses the pair; `Bottom` lies within both bounds and cannot be written, so which path moves is his. The POPL 2019 rules map reads the paper's rules on it, by reading only: [Meet-Excl] goes through existential reduction, which collects the "constraints C that make α different from Bottom" (`Papers/Variance/rules.tex:343-345`), with `unify` and `toBounds` named but given no rules (`rules.tex:252-258`), and no instance is `Bottom` (`rules.tex:159`; `resolve.tex:239-241`, `:773-774`). If `unify` fails on the merged parameter, whose only instance would be `Bottom`, the meet stays unreduced and [Exc-Object-Same] over the two parameters gives exclusion, so the pair is valid; if it returns the merged parameter bounded by both, the pair is refused. The rules state neither, and the Working Draft left the same point open (`Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/future.tex:265`). Its two ways are this item's: the checker's reduction treats an existential whose parameter's bounds meet only at `Bottom` as empty and agrees with walk, or walk's `mayBeEqual` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:1448-1472`) admits `Bottom` as the two parameters' common argument and refuses the pair at load as the checker does; neither alone keeps today's behaviour (`reviews/popl2019-rules-map.md`, question 1).
   - Landed: The checker as it is: yes for a named forced argument, and it cannot conclude it through ancestors (the `CAP` shape); for `tint`, both paths as they are, row 786 `CONTESTED`. The text names the question in Appendix I's "Passages not yet revised".
   - The other way: The text answers it: rung S's "no", which the gather removed, or a "yes"; and walk refuses `tint`, or the checker accepts it.
   - Its cost: A sentence of the overloading chapter, and a walk rung or a checker rung to match it.
   - Home: PLAN, "Climb batch 7b, listed for his review", Whether two parameter types exclude each other when the; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/SKEPTIC.md:140` (10-02: 31); PLAN, "Climb batch 19, listed for his review", P.worker.1 and P.skeptic.1; row 786; POSITIONS-history, P-152, its block of 2026-10-22 08:30Z, the former "Left:" list, which named `tint` (row 786); `reviews/popl2019-rules-map.md`, question 1 and sections 11, 16 and 18
   - Needed by: before the tint rung (row 786); climb batch 21's candidates hold the row for his answer (PLAN, "Off the path, parked", "Phase 3's candidates at its end"), and item 192 writes a sentence in the same passage of `overloading.tex`.

323. **P-60's coverage against the POPL 2019 paper's Meet Rule: does the meet of two overloads over closed traits stay covered by several declarations, or does it take one declaration, as [Meet-Third] and the paper's theorem of one most specific declaration ask (P-60)?** The rule: a pair whose domains overlap and do not nest needs a third declaration whose domain is equivalent to their meet, [Meet-Third] (`Papers/Variance/rules.tex:57-61`), so that every call has one most specific declaration statically (`thm:mostspecific`, `rules.tex:509-524`). The decision: P-60 lets several declarations below both cover the meet through `comprises` clauses, so a static call may have several most specific declarations, typed by the intersection of their return types, the declaration that runs unique only at run time (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md:57`); the checker builds it for declarations without static parameters (`coverageRule`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:676-694`; `coversOverlap`, `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala:188-239`). The type-decisions judgement of 2026-10-23 weighed it: "P-60 is the one step outside the designers' proven model, and it is recorded as such; it stands" (`reviews/type-decisions-review/judgement.md`, V6), and Appendix I says so (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3514-3525`). The POPL 2019 rules map, read against the technical report's sources, sets the rule beside P-60 as a decision not taken, with the same two ways (`reviews/popl2019-rules-map.md`, question 2, sections 18 and 23). The Working Draft's passage that the other way cites ends "We agreed to revise the Meet rule to address this with the coverage check." (`Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/future.tex:285`), which Appendix I quotes (`changes.tex:3485`).
   - Landed: P-60 as it reads, its coverage case built in the checker. Default: P-60 as it reads.
